# The Garmin client fixtures

`expected.json` is **the Python reference implementation's own output**, not a
transcription of it. It is regenerated by:

```bash
STRIDE_DATA_DIR=/tmp/stride-golden backend/.venv/bin/python \
    crates/stride-garmin/tests/fixtures/make_expected.py
```

The script imports the reference implementation — it does not modify it — and
calls its functions:

| expectation | reference function |
|---|---|
| `profile.athlete_name` | `app.api.auth._athlete_from_personal` |
| `activity_detail`, `activity_detail_fallback`, `activity_list` | `app.services.personal_sync._canonical_from_detail` |
| `lists.*` | `app.ingest.garmin_personal._as_list` |
| `dates.*` | `app.ingest.garmin_personal._bounded_date_range` |
| `activities_params.*` | `app.ingest.garmin_personal.GarminPersonalClient.activities` — the client is called with its HTTP call replaced by a capture, so the expectation is the query the reference itself computes |
| `zones` | `app.services.fingerprint.zone_model` — the zone model the reference builds from the biometric payload |

`activities_params` pins the clamps the reference applies to an activity
search: `start` is capped at 299, `limit` at 100 and at `300 - start`, and the
window is clamped to a year. The port had two of these wrong and the golden
set found both.

`lists_bare_array` and `lists_unknown_envelope` pin `_as_list` on a payload
that is not an envelope at all (the array is taken) and on one whose envelope
the reference does not know (nothing is taken).

The `*.json` files beside it are the Garmin payloads the expectations are
computed from. They are hand-written, but every field in them is a field the
reference implementation reads, so a field the reference ignores cannot hide a
mistake in the port.

The Rust test that consumes them is `crates/stride-garmin/tests/golden_parity.rs`.
It compares with the rule of `docs/core-contract.md` §8: strings, booleans,
null and integers exactly; floating point numbers within
`1e-9 × max(1, |golden value|)`.

Two things the reference does that the port has to copy:

* the reference reads the activity's numbers from the **detail** payload and
  uses the list item only as a fallback for the id, the name and the start
  time — so `activity_detail_fallback.json` deliberately has neither a name
  nor a start time, and both come from the list item;
* the reference renders a UTC start time as `+00:00`, never `Z`.

And two things the reference does that the port had wrong:

* the zone rows are read as `zoneLowBoundary`/`zoneHighBoundary` and
  `zoneNumber`, and a zone's name is `name` — Garmin's own `zoneName` is not
  read, so the names are `Zone 1` to `Zone 5`;
* the zone model's field names are the reference's own (`zone_no`, `name`,
  `low_bpm`, `high_bpm`), because that is the shape the reference reads back
  out of the athlete's stored zones.

## Why these are not in `backend/tests/golden/`

The golden fixtures there are the FIT parser's and the domain's; the cases are
inputs to `stride-fit` and `stride-core` and their expected outputs are
produced from a FIT file. A Garmin client cannot be checked against them —
there is no client case and no client output file. This directory is the
crate's own golden set, and `crates/*/tests/golden/**` belongs to the
orchestrator's W9 workstream, so nothing was written there.
